svg.title: Exact versus approximate nearest-neighbor search
svg.desc: Items are points in an embedding space, so finding similar items means finding the nearest points. Exact search computes the distance from the query to all 34 items. A graph-based ANN search such as HNSW hops along neighbor links toward the query, computes only 11 distances, and here finds the same 3 nearest items. It can occasionally miss one, but it stays fast even with billions of items.
svg.text: Finding the closest items without checking them all
Dot = an item's embedding. Close dots = similar items.
always exact · grows with every item
same 3 found · may rarely miss one
A few hops instead of a full scan: milliseconds, even for billions.
